name: Embryonal Tumor of Neuroepithelial Tissue

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of small round blue cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio on histology
Positive staining for neuronal markers such as synaptophysin and neuron-specific enolase
Detection of characteristic genetic alterations such as amplification of MYC or alterations in LIN28A
MRI showing a well-demarcated, often enhancing mass in the CNS

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with immunohistochemical positivity and molecular genetic evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular genetics per WHO CNS tumor guidelines.

laboratory: CSF cytology may show malignant cells in metastatic cases
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in serum or CSF
imaging: MRI brain showing heterogeneously enhancing mass with possible necrosis
Evidence of peritumoral edema and mass effect
other: Histopathology demonstrating small round blue cells with high mitotic index
Immunohistochemical positivity for synaptophysin, NSE, and sometimes GFAP

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic alterations such as CTNNB1 mutations
Loss of INI1 (SMARCB1) expression on immunohistochemistry
Different histopathological features with rhabdoid cells

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
New onset seizures in a child or young adult
